entries.name: No Child Left Behind Act
entries.definition: A United States federal education law from the early 2000s that set testing and accountability requirements for public schools and was replaced in 2015 by the Every Student Succeeds Act.

entries.name: Node.js
entries.definition: A cross-platform JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that runs JavaScript outside the browser.

entries.name: Non-Facility Associated Signalling
entries.definition: An ISDN primary rate interface arrangement in which a single D channel carries the signalling for several PRI trunk groups.

entries.name: Non-fungible tokens
entries.definition: Unique blockchain-based tokens that record ownership of a digital or physical item.

entries.name: Nonverbal communication
entries.definition: Conveying and reading meaning without words, through body language, gestures, facial expression and tone.

entries.name: nosetests
entries.definition: The command-line test runner of nose, a Python unit testing framework that extends unittest.

entries.name: NoSQL database
entries.definition: A database that stores data in non-relational models such as documents, key-value pairs, columns or graphs.

entries.name: Notion (software)
entries.definition: A workspace app for notes, documents, wikis and databases.

entries.name: npm
entries.definition: The default package manager for Node.js, used to install and manage JavaScript packages.

entries.name: Nuance PDF Converter
entries.definition: Nuance software for creating, converting and editing PDF files.

entries.name: NumPy
entries.definition: A Python library for fast numerical computing built around N-dimensional arrays.

entries.name: NuoDB
entries.definition: A distributed SQL relational database designed to run in the cloud.

entries.name: Nutanix
entries.definition: A hyperconverged infrastructure platform that combines compute, storage and virtualisation on clustered servers.

entries.name: Nutanix AHV
entries.definition: Nutanix's built-in hypervisor, based on KVM, that runs virtual machines on Nutanix clusters.

entries.name: Nutanix Calm
entries.definition: Nutanix's application automation and orchestration tool for provisioning and managing applications across clouds.

entries.name: Nutanix Prism
entries.definition: Nutanix's web-based console for monitoring and managing Nutanix clusters.

entries.name: Nutraceuticals
entries.definition: Food-derived products, such as supplements and fortified foods, that are sold for health benefits beyond basic nutrition.

entries.name: Nutrition care planning
entries.definition: Writing individual plans that set a patient's nutrition goals, interventions and follow-up.

entries.name: Nutrition consulting
entries.definition: Advising individuals or organisations on diet and eating habits to meet health or performance goals.

entries.name: Nutrition diagnosis
entries.definition: The step of the Nutrition Care Process in which a dietitian identifies and names a nutrition problem that they are responsible for treating.

entries.name: Nutrition intervention
entries.definition: The step of the Nutrition Care Process in which planned actions are taken to address an identified nutrition problem.

entries.name: Nutritional assessment
entries.definition: Evaluating a person's nutritional status from diet history, body measurements, clinical signs and laboratory results.

entries.name: Nutritional screening
entries.definition: Quickly identifying people who are malnourished or at nutritional risk, using a short validated screening tool.

entries.name: Nuxt
entries.definition: A framework built on Vue.js for building server-rendered and static web applications.

entries.name: NW.js
entries.definition: A framework for building desktop applications with HTML, CSS and JavaScript on top of Node.js and Chromium.

entries.name: OBD-II
entries.definition: A standard for on-board vehicle diagnostics that gives access to a car's engine and emissions data through a standard connector and fault codes.

entries.name: Object-oriented data model
entries.definition: A way of modelling data in which information is represented as objects that have attributes and behaviour and can be related to one another.
variants: Object-Oriented Data Model For Database Modelling

entries.name: Object-oriented design
entries.definition: Designing software using objects and their relationships.

entries.name: Object-oriented programming
entries.definition: A programming paradigm that organises code into objects that combine data and the behaviour that works on it.

entries.name: Observability
entries.definition: Inspecting system behavior using recorded evidence such as logs, traces and metrics.

entries.name: OCLC Connexion
entries.definition: OCLC's cataloguing service and client software for creating and editing library catalogue records.

entries.name: Ocular pathology
entries.definition: The branch of pathology that studies diseases of the eye and the tissues around it.

entries.name: OCUnit
entries.definition: A unit testing framework for Objective-C that was bundled with Apple's Xcode before XCTest replaced it.

entries.name: Odor control
entries.definition: Methods and equipment, such as scrubbers and biofilters, for removing or neutralising unpleasant odours in plants such as wastewater and industrial facilities.

entries.name: Office 365
entries.definition: Microsoft's subscription service that provides Office applications such as Word, Excel and Outlook together with cloud services for email, file storage and collaboration; many plans are now sold as Microsoft 365.

entries.name: Office and productivity software
entries.definition: Software for everyday office work, such as word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and email.

entries.name: Official statistics
entries.definition: Statistics produced and published by government statistical agencies about a country's population, economy and society.

entries.name: Ohm's law
entries.definition: The law that the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it, written V = I × R.

entries.name: Oil pipelines
entries.definition: The pipeline systems that carry crude oil and refined products, and the engineering, operation and regulation of them.

entries.name: omniORB
entries.definition: An open-source CORBA object request broker for C++ and Python.
